archetypes.name: surface-completeness
archetypes.rationale: The plan promises a completeness grep gate over the full live surface but lists only 13 files; verify no occurrences of the retired argv token linger in unlisted files such as skills/shared/, agents/, topology.tsv, alias definitions, or any .toml/.txt/.sh not enumerated in the plan.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan retires a public argv token and asserts that a completeness grep over the full live surface must return zero rows, but it lists only 13 files to update. Search beyond those 13 files — including skills/shared/ markdown, agents/ prompt files, skills/*/references/ directories not in the list, topology.tsv, .toml config, and any alias or hook definition — for any occurrence of the retired argv token that is not covered by the plan's explicit excluded paths (larch-logs/, .git/, CHANGELOG.md). For each hit, determine whether the plan's proposed edits would actually eliminate it or whether it is a genuinely uncovered location requiring an additional edit step. Pay particular attention to surfaces that cross-reference the flag table (e.g. topology projection rows, plugin.json description fields beyond the one listed). Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: outcome-lifecycle
archetypes.rationale: cancelled-tier-gate is retired on the assumption that the interactive gate is its sole producer; verify that claim holds across all SKILL.md files, scripts, audit tooling, and log-parsing surfaces not in the file list, and that every consumer site is accounted for in the plan.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan retires the SUMMARY_OUTCOME value cancelled-tier-gate by removing its claimed sole producer, but this claim is asserted rather than traced through the codebase. Search all SKILL.md files, shell scripts under scripts/ and skills/, and any audit or log-parsing code (including the audit-runs skill and larch-logs tooling) for occurrences of that outcome string to confirm no other producer exists and no consumer is missed by the plan. Verify that the plan's retirement sites — the SKILL enum, renderer case branch, renderer test, and run-summary doc table — form a complete closure and that no outcome-aware downstream (e.g. write-run-params.sh validation, read-design-classification.sh, or the run-log batch schema) needs a corresponding update. Also check whether any other skill or doc references the interactive tier gate by name in a way that would become stale after this change. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: default-promotion-drift
archetypes.rationale: The change shifts observable UX from interactive-prompt to silent auto-SIMPLE; verify that every user-facing prose surface consistently describes the new default and that no remnant still implies an interactive tier choice or mixes old and new tier-selection language.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan replaces an interactive AskUserQuestion tier gate with a silent auto-SIMPLE resolution, which changes the observable behavior for every /design invocation that omits a tier flag. Check each listed user-facing file — SKILL.md, flags.md, approval-gates.md, README.md, docs/skills.md, docs/workflow-lifecycle.md, docs/installation-and-setup.md, docs/issue-anchored-plan.md — for any prose that still describes or implies an interactive tier choice, mixed-tense descriptions, or argument-hint strings that do not match the new single-flag model. Verify that the Step 0b sub-step numbering in SKILL.md remains internally consistent after renaming the gate step to tier resolution, and that the resume-path skip list and Anti-halt reminder reference only step labels that will still exist in the updated skill. Identify any argument-hint or flag table entry that still implies a user prompt where none will occur. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
